note: Hardening the boot after a multi-repo web session found no .venv and no injected seat and walked straight past the cold-start (IDEAS §6.108). Root cause: every hook in .claude/settings.json was addressed as `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/hooks/nestor-hook`, the runtime left CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR unset, so the command expanded to a nonexistent `/hooks/nestor-hook` and no-op'd under the runner's check=False — the same silent-abort class as decision 0054, one layer up (the invocation, not the script body). The docs (confirmed against code.claude.com) say CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is 'always set' and settings are discovered by git-repo resolution, but a session rooted at a NON-git parent of sibling repos is an undocumented edge, and that is where it broke.

decisions.question: The boot depends on a runtime variable (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR) that was unset. Fix by trusting it harder, or by not trusting it at all?
decisions.commitment: Not at all. hooks/nestor-hook and .claude/hooks/session-start.sh now resolve their repo root from their own file location (readlink -f on ${BASH_SOURCE[0]}, then ../ or ../../), with NESTOR_PROJECT_ROOT kept only as an explicit test override. Neither script reads CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR or $PWD to find the repo anymore.
decisions.why: A script's own path is the one anchor that is correct regardless of cwd, of which repo in a multi-repo checkout the session is rooted at, or of which variables the runtime chose to set. $PWD is the parent in a multi-repo web session and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR was simply absent; both are things done TO the script, and a boot step that hinges on them fails exactly when the layout is unusual. Verified: invoked from /tmp with all three project vars stripped, nestor-hook still produces the correct seat and the MCP deny, and session-start.sh still names the real repo root rather than /tmp.

decisions.question: settings.json still has to name nestor-hook somehow, and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR may be unset. What path does it use?
decisions.commitment: A POSIX resolver, not a bare variable: `for b in "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-}" "$PWD"; do d="$b"; while [ -n "$d" ]; do [ -x "$d/hooks/nestor-hook" ] && exec "$d/hooks/nestor-hook" claude <module>; [ "$d" = / ] && break; d=$(dirname "$d"); done; done`. It prefers the variable when set, else walks up from the working directory, and no-ops cleanly (exit 0) when it finds nothing.
decisions.why: Self-location fixes the script once it is REACHED; this is what reaches it. It recovers every case that has an anchor the hook can see — var set and correct, var unset with cwd at the repo, cwd drifted into a subdir, and even a var pointing at the parent — measured across all four. It cannot invent an anchor that is not there, so it does not error the turn when there is none; it declines quietly, the same posture the runner already takes.

decisions.question: Does the resolver close the hole completely?
decisions.commitment: No, and it says so. A session rooted ABOVE the repo with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR unset (the exact multi-repo web layout that produced §6.108) has no anchor pointing into the sibling subdir, so no project-scoped hook command can locate itself from there. Recorded as the residual in §6.108 and left to the runtime, not papered over.
decisions.why: Overclaiming a fix is the failure this repo refuses more than it refuses the bug. The honest boundary is: the boot now survives an unset variable whenever the hook is invoked with cwd at or under the repo, which is the single-repo web case and the common drift cases; the parent-rooted multi-repo case is a platform gap (undocumented per the Claude Code docs) whose real fix is upstream — rooting the session at the repo, or a setup script the runtime runs before launch.

decisions.question: The bootstrap failed silently once already. How does the next failure announce itself?
decisions.commitment: session-start.sh is loud on both non-outcomes: it prints to stderr (naming the resolved repo root) when it declines because CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE != true, and exits non-zero after building if no interpreter landed at .venv/bin/python; it also warns when it built a venv but CLAUDE_ENV_FILE was unset so PATH could not be updated. The agent-facing signal is unchanged and independent: session_start's `[check] pytest:` line already reports a missing .venv.
decisions.why: FINDINGS-2026-08-12 §1.1: a setup step that declines is a different thing from one that ran, and a silent `exit 0` was indistinguishable from success — which is the cold-clone trap the script exists to prevent, arriving through the script itself. A gate nobody can watch fail is a decoration; the new test breaks the wiring on purpose (the bare `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/...` form) and watches it 127.
